claims.text: The release datelined 'From the Office of thr Primer Minister, Nuku'alofa, 30 Jul 2008' [as printed] says that the King's traditional installation at the taumafa kava ceremony 'took place today (July 30th)' at Pangai Lahi, near the royal palace. It is issued by Tu'ivanuavou, Keeper of the Palace Records and Master of the Royal Household, on 30 July 2008.
claims.locator: Dateline and first paragraph; issuing line at the end
claims.uncertainty: Post-event occurrence record for the traditional installation. The venue is named Pangai Lahi here and Mala'e Pangai in the programme (to_crown_gtv_taumafa_kava_scheduled_20080730); both names are kept as printed.

claims.text: The same release reports that the talking chief Motu'apuaka declared at the ceremony that from that moment His Majesty became King of Tonga, and it says that to Tongans the taumafa kava was King George's true coronation.
claims.locator: Paragraph 2 and the paragraph before the closing acclamation
claims.uncertainty: A customary declaration and a cultural characterisation, reported by the palace. They are not the constitutional accession, which followed from the devolution of the Crown on 11 September 2006 (TO-CROWN-04), nor the church coronation of 1 August 2008, and they are not used as a start date.
